A1.justification: Both PDFs describe AdaFisher, with matching core algorithms, theoretical results, and benchmark results. Their text, equations, tables, figures, and appendices support reliable comparison, including material moved or renumbered in v2.

before.justification: v1 reports original image-classification, transfer-learning, and WikiText-2 experiments, plus optimizer stability and Fisher-structure analyses in the appendices.

after.justification: v2 retains those original experiments and adds Penn Treebank results, distributed ImageNet experiments, and component and Fisher-approximation analyses.

M1.justification: Algorithm 1 and the core diagonal-Fisher, normalization, momentum, and EMA procedures remain unchanged. Appendix A.4 adds a distributed adaptation that averages normalized Kronecker factors across GPUs before constructing the preconditioner.

E1.justification: v2 adds Penn Treebank language-model evaluation in Section 4.3 and a MNIST subset for Fisher-approximation diagnostics in Appendix B.2. Existing image-classification, language-modeling, and IRIS visualization coverage is retained. Larger batches and multiple GPUs change settings rather than dataset coverage.

E2.justification: The established benchmark comparator sets are retained, including KFAC renamed K-FAC. The new component experiment in Figure 13(A) adds square-root-free Adam as a comparator against AdaFisher variants; this is an evaluated modification rather than merely a citation.

E3.justification: v1 describes recommended/default settings for several CNN baselines; v2 reports learning-rate searches across optimizers and broader damping, Hessian-power, and decay-factor searches in Appendix D.2.1. This changes the reported protocol without establishing that retained experiments were rerun. New protocols also include distributed GPU/batch configurations, scheduler and component controls, and a 50-epoch MNIST reference-Fisher comparison using MAE.

E4.justification: Beyond the retained spectral, batch-size, learning-rate, and cutout analyses, new Appendix B directly tests schedulers, square-root omission, EMA, and normalization-layer Fisher computation. It adds Adam/AdaFisher Fisher-distribution diagnostics and comparison with a reference Fisher diagonal. Appendices A.4 and D.2.4 additionally examine distributed scaling and larger-batch behavior.

E5.justification: Appendix B.2 newly reports Monte Carlo sampling for estimating the reference Fisher, adding a statistical estimation procedure without specifying its sample count. The existing five-initialization CIFAR mean/standard-deviation reporting and single-trial Tiny ImageNet/ImageNet practice remain unchanged; additional repeated training runs are not established.

E6.justification: Matched existing benchmark table values are unchanged. New results include PTB perplexities of 41.15 for AdaFisherW, 44.70 for AdamW, and 59.43 for AdaHessian (Table 4); ImageNet top-1 accuracies of 77.01 and 77.09 at batches 512 and 1024 (Figure 5); and distributed timing, ablation, and Fisher-diagnostic results. These are added results under new conditions, not same-setting improvements over v1.

T1.justification: Appendix A.4 adds a conditional unbiasedness argument for averaging distributed Kronecker-factor estimates, using linearity of expectation. Section 2 makes the model-output distribution in the Fisher expectation explicit. The existing convex/nonconvex propositions, convergence bounds, and appendix proofs remain substantially unchanged.

C1.justification: The core optimizer and performance claims are retained. v2 adds an explainable Fisher measure to the stated contributions and extends the ImageNet conclusion to multi-GPU training. The introduction also drops v1's explicit restriction of the diagonal-energy finding to the examined architectures, layers, and losses.

C2.justification: The existing Fisher/Hessian convergence explanation moves to Appendix B.1. New discussion interprets Fisher histograms and component effects, and qualifies square-root-free Adam comparisons through a batch-size scaling requirement. v2 removes the distributed-training limitation, expands the caveat about literature ImageNet settings and augmentations, and drops the architecture-specific diagonal-dominance qualification.

D1.justification: v2 substantially expands tuning documentation with damping, Hessian-power, and decay-factor search grids, and documents distributed hardware use and NNgeometry-based diagnostic procedures. It revises the available GPU inventory from eight to six and removes the experimental appendix's previously selected decay-factor pair. Selected learning-rate tables and the code-access link remain unchanged; some final parameter selections remain unspecified.

R1.justification: v2 adds references for MNIST (Deng, 2012), Penn Treebank (Marcus et al., 1993), NNgeometry (George, 2021), and normalization (Jiang et al., 2024b). Section 5 largely retains the earlier positioning relative to Fisher approximations and adaptive optimizers. Expanded author names and bibliography formatting do not represent additional works.

P1.justification: The main section sequence and much existing prose are preserved. v2 adds a methodology roadmap, selectively rewrites contributions, stability discussion, and conclusions, and reorganizes tuning details into lists. The impact statement moves into the main text, while the visualization and experiment appendices shift after the new ablation appendix.

P2.justification: v2 adds Fisher histograms, scheduler/component plots, distributed-training displays, and an ablation-summary table; expands the language-model table and plot for PTB; redraws Figure 2; and changes the document template and display placement. Most existing benchmark plots are retained. New presentation errors include Figure 13's caption describing panel A as the MAE analysis, which is actually panel D.

improvement.justification: Appendix B substantially strengthens evidence for design choices that v1 supported mainly indirectly, through controlled EMA, square-root, and normalization-layer ablations plus Fisher-approximation diagnostics. Appendix A.4 specifies and tests distributed training, addressing an explicit v1 limitation. These gains outweigh incomplete tuning selections, new caption/reference errors, and weakened caution about diagonal dominance. The improvement comes from stronger validation and documented applicability, while matched benchmark scores remain unchanged.
